items.title: Stuart Bergen Interview, 1970-07-18
items.q: That was the only time I ever played with Pete. And Pete played the first night, that Saturday night. And it was me and Pete and Joe Rodas in the front line

ctx.x: Okay, it's going on the fourth reel now, Barry.

Dick, around 1954 I remember. Basin Street Six had really split up. I think Gerard formed his own band, but Pete and Joe Rodas, Bonnie Franks, they kept that name, Basin Street Six. And they were playing I think where Soul City is today, on Jefferson Highway, Airline Highway. And their regular band was Connie Jones was playing trumpet instead of George, and they had Johnny Edwards on drums instead of Charlie Duke. Outside of that the band was the same. But this kid Connie Jones had to go to National Guard, and…
While we're talking about different things we didn't get into Lester Nelson very much. He's a guy that I hear people talk about and don't know much about him.

items.title: Stuart Bergen Interview, 1970-07-18
items.q: And Muscat rambles out of this world man. It's terrific. And I think I like that better than that. They have good teamwork too. The band hits it off good with him...

ctx.x: And Muscat rambles out of this world man. It's terrific. And I think I like that better than that. They have good teamwork too. The band hits it off good with him and he plays a lot of good. Of course he throws in a few little tunes but he dresses them up so nice that they're jazzy. They're not just inserting a couple of measures of another tune. He makes them fit in right. I used to always like Someday You'll Be Sorry. I thought it was very fine. And I have a lot of records that you're probably not up on like…
A little bamboo bridge. To you sweetheart. He plays good stuff.
